correctness.rationale: At any common squared radius x the monomial Gram diagonal is fixed. The inverse diagonal bound, with equality exactly for a diagonal Gram matrix, reduces the risk to F(x)=(1−x)^(−p)∑ b_k x^(−k). Vanishing first N Fourier moments make the square weighted Vandermonde matrix unitary: row norms force uniform weights, and pairwise row orthogonality forces regular polygon sites up to rotation. The derivative of the log risk at t=−log x is the tilted mean of k minus p/(exp(t)−1), strictly increasing by positivity of the variance and with limits −∞ and N. For L=Nt and 1<p<2 the weighted Riemann integrals have integrable lower endpoints, and bracket L_N by the strictly monotone equation in the finding. At p=2 the harmonic sum at L=log log N+c remains asymptotic to log N (its excess is O(exp(L)/L+L)); the exact stationarity right side is asymptotic to exp(c) log N/2. For p>2 and L=(p−2)log N+c, the beta integral gives total un-tilted mass B=(p−1)/(p−2); the local upper-end scale N/L gives S'_N∼Γ(p)exp(c)N/L. Its contribution to S_N is O(1/L); below a small fixed fraction of N the derivative bound is o(N/L), and the middle block is smaller by a power of N than the leading derivative term. Thus S_N→B, giving the claimed constant shift by bracketing at fixed c. Substituting all three radius laws into F verifies the stated risk constants. Independent checks corroborate angular optimality, exact N=1,p=2 radius x=1/4, and finite solutions for three exponents, including slow convergence at p=2.
residual_risks: The common radius is optimized but different simultaneous radii are not allowed. The budget and full kernel normalization are essential.
Finite numerical checks do not establish an asymptotic constant or supply effective rates of convergence.

originality.rationale: The regular-polygon geometry and angular Fourier rigidity are already known in closely related optimal circle designs; the angular step is a standard consequence of fixed Gram diagonals and diagonalization. The supported distinct claim is the A-risk radial optimization with full weighted Bergman kernel normalization, especially the sharp transition across p=2 and the sharp risk constants. The strongest nearby theorem minimizes a scale-invariant extremal-eigenvalue ratio on a larger class but gives a different optimizer and no equivalent inverse-trace asymptotic law.
residual_risks: Bounded priority search; an unlocated optimal-design result may cover more of the A-risk radial calculation.
The same-day angular analogue does not establish ordering of publication.

value.rationale: Inverse trace measures total coefficient-recovery variance in the whitened weighted observation model. With the minimal sufficient number of positive sites under full-kernel scaling, the sharp transition tells a designer where to put the only sampling circle and what total inverse-information growth to expect. The summability change produces three genuinely different radial scales, especially the slow critical double logarithm, not merely a relabeling of a condition-number optimizer.
residual_risks: Design restricted to one common circle and the given normalization. No performance guarantee for arbitrary noise, freely varying radii, or a uniform-in-p crossover is asserted.
